correctness.rationale: The dual has exactly all singleton/pair faces, induced-path triples, and facial-square tetrahedra, with no larger faces by Mantel. The no-K_{2,3} condition makes the prescribed tetrahedron/triangle and isolated path-triangle removals genuine elementary free-face collapses. Counting leaves precisely the triangulated surface and q=binom(N,2)-sum binom(deg(v),2) unattached-to-triangles chords; attaching chords adds independent circles. Integral surface cohomology and Alexander duality give the stated degree N-5 free or 2-torsion class and degree N-4 free rank, all other zero. Infinite twisted family satisfies minimum-deck-displacement ≥7 and quotient Klein geometry. Standalone exact four-case verifier replayed; finite ranks are supplementary, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary and closely related full-text sources, published indexed claims, equivalent formulations and broader-theorem implications. Earlier ordinary cut-complex graph results do not cover edge-sharing closed quadrangulations; open grids are not closed surfaces; toroidal prior is orientable special case; a same-graph Klein Rips theorem uses a different simplicial functor. The general closed-surface orientability transfer and infinite ordinary-three-cut Z/2 family are not implied by inspected sources. Equivalent unindexed work remains possible.
residual_risks: No indexed literature search guarantees absolute novelty; alternative unindexed Alexander-dual or hypergraph formulations may contain equivalent theorems.
Classification is conditional on every 4-cycle being facial and no K_{2,3}; broad unconditional quadrangulation extensions are not claimed.

value.rationale: An exact integral classification of a natural class of topologically embedded graph complexes detects surface orientability through a forced Z/2 class, not visible in rational Betti numbers or the prior orientable torus case. It yields complete integral homology and nonshellability for all eligible genus types, with an explicit two-parameter Klein-bottle torsion family and transparent collapse mechanism. These are nonroutine structural phenomena rather than a renamed or arbitrary one-off computation.
